status: SKELETON -- empty plumbing (corpus.realWorldExamples == []). Trans genesis K159; forked from the RTD RWE schema (sibling vendoring of the flagship RWE family, sized down). instance_polarity/attestation_status/subject_type value-sets enforced by transgenderism_validator_v0_1.py (check_rwe). Data populated downstream (append-only); none fabricated.

parent_family.relation: Sibling vendoring of the flagship RWE family for anchor + export-discipline compatibility, sized down for a small library. Heavier attestation fields (archetype_signal_* / frame_inversion / layer_skepticism / public_reach / refutation_variant_id) are INHERITABLE FROM THE PARENT per record when needed — NOT required at launch.

anchor_discipline: instance_id values are APPEND-ONLY deep-link anchors (recommended rwe-<id> family) — never recycled, mirroring the objection #obj-<id> covenant.
binding: RWE records live in corpus.realWorldExamples[]. Each attaches to >=1 objection via attached_objections[].objection_id (foreign key into corpus.objections[].id). Objection nodes carry rwe_refs[] as the reverse slot (an array of instance_id).

example_record_schema._doc: Core/lighter record fields, sized down from the flagship example_record_schema; extend from the parent as a record needs it. instance_polarity/attestation_status/subject_type carry explicit enforced value-sets (validator-checked). recovery_status is STRUCK (see struck_fields).

archive_url._doc: corpus-decay hedge; recommended for fragile sources

instance_polarity._doc: Replaces the prior values_ref:parent. Its main driver (recovery-after-intervention cases) is gone with recovery_status; temporary-problem itself ships empty or neutral-illustration only. Other nodes may still carry genuinely two-sided cases. 'contested' (4th value, added v0.2.2) = one source cited by BOTH sides (e.g. an official report read as evidence by disability-rights critics AND disputed by MAiD-supportive analysts).

subject_type._doc: Enforcement discriminator. subject_type == real-person triggers the attestation requirement.

attestation_status._doc: Real-person records: REQUIRED and must not be 'unverified' ('unverified' blocks the record). The responsible-citation spine — independent of the (struck) futility question.

validation_rules._doc: Core rules vendored from the parent + the v0.2 enforcement set. Implemented in transgenderism_validator_v0_1.py (check_rwe): PRESENCE checks (subject_type + instance_polarity required on every record) + enum checks on instance_polarity/attestation_status/subject_type; subject_type==real-person requires attestation_status != unverified. VACUOUS while realWorldExamples == []; engages automatically when RWE data lands. NO recovery_status checks.
rules: v4_foreign_key_validity — attached_objections[].objection_id resolves to corpus objections[].id
rwe_refs_resolve — every objection.rwe_refs[] resolves to a realWorldExamples[].instance_id (both directions)
subject_type_required — subject_type present on EVERY record (FAIL if absent; the real-person attestation guard)
instance_polarity_required — instance_polarity present on every record (per required:true)
real_person_attestation_required — subject_type==real-person => attestation_status present AND != unverified

struck_fields.recovery_status: STRUCK for this library (trans, K159). Not applicable to an optionality-only register: the library makes no therapeutic/outcome claim (the Firewall forbids it), so no treatment-futility / regret-outcome field enters. Do NOT add recovery_status to records or the validator.

rules: public-record only; no private individuals, no reconstructing a private person's case
attestation required + truthful on real-person records (unverified -> flag/FAIL)
no medical means/protocols, ever -- policy / population / clinical-outcome level only
no exhortation -- a record illustrates an empirical claim; never a model anyone should follow
catalogue the inverse honestly (general suite discipline)
conservative attribution -- verify subject/case at authoring; categories hold regardless
